answer: Each agent identity can be tied to a persistent, costly stake that is slashed when it signs conflicting work or fails a randomly sampled task. A reputation anchor records verified history, while a ridge in the stake requirement makes creating many identities more expensive than concentrating value in one. The attacker must lock real capital per identity and risk losing it; an ivory label or fresh account cannot cheaply multiply influence. This raises the cost of a sybil swarm without claiming to make attacks impossible.
